title: POC wrap: latency & cost wins + quick reference ask
text:
POC wrap: latency & cost wins + quick reference ask

['From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@fathomlogistics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC wrap: latency & cost wins + quick reference ask

Hi Ellen —

Thanks again for running the POC with us last week. Quick recap of the measurable wins we saw in your environment over the three-week run (attached slides):

- Average 95th-pctt latency for end-user requests dropped from ~420ms to ~160ms.
- Per-token inference cost reduced ~38% using batching + KV cache on the same model.
- Successful handling of 8k concurrent user sessions during stress window with no errors.

Those results are exactly what our ops team was hoping to validate — robust tail-latency and meaningful unit-cost improvements without changing your model code.

Would Fathom be open to two small asks?
1) A one-line quote we can use on a case blurb (we can draft it for you and you can edit).
2) A 15-minute reference call with one of your product leaders next week so we can put together a short case study (not marketing heavy — focused on technical impact).

If you’re open to both, I attached the slides + a quick draft quote to make it easy. Suggested times for a 15-min sync: Tue 3/9 10:00–11:00 PT or Wed 3/10 14:00–15:00 PT.

Thanks — appreciate your partnership.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Dylan.Brooks@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0123

Cc: Samir Khan <samir.khan@fathomlogistics.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 11:08:21 -0800
Subject: Re: POC wrap: latency & cost wins + quick reference ask

Dylan —

Really appreciate the clear recap and the slides. The improvements look great and align with what we observed on our side. Samir and I reviewed the numbers and we're comfortable moving forward with a short quote and a brief reference call.

A couple of notes:
- Please keep the quote short and technical (one line) — Samir will want it specific to latency and cost.
- For legal/marketing: I'll need our procurement team to sign off on logo usage. I can get that approved if you send a one-paragraph blurb and a sample logo consent.

We can do Tue 3/9 at 10:15 PT — that works for both of us.

Can you send the one-line draft and the short agenda for the 15-min call?

Thanks,
Ellen
Ellen Park
Head of Product — Edge Systems
Fathom Logistics
ellen.park@fathomlogistics.com
(617) 444-2217", 'From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: POC wrap: latency & cost wins + quick reference ask

Ellen — thanks, great to hear.

Attached is a short draft one-line quote and a proposed 15-min agenda. Feel free to edit:

Draft one-line quote (editable):
“Using Redwood’s inference runtime, Fathom reduced 95th-percentile inference latency by ~62% while cutting per-token cost by roughly 38% during our POC.”

15-min agenda (Tue 3/9 10:15 PT):
- 10:15–10:18: Quick intros and context (Dylan, Marissa, Ellen, Samir)
- 10:18–10:23: Fathom confirms outcomes & any clarifying notes
- 10:23–10:28: Next steps for case study, logo consent, and publishing timeline

I attached the draft quote as redwood-draft-quote.txt and the slides again for reference. If the draft looks good, Ellen, can you confirm: 1) if we can publish that line attributed to Fathom Logistics, and 2) whether procurement needs a specific consent template (happy to share our short consent form).

—Dylan

Quick note from CS side: if you prefer, we can provide a very short consent template that we use for technical case studies (one paragraph + logo checkbox). That usually satisfies procurement and speeds approvals.

If Tue 3/9 10:15 PT still works, I’ll send a calendar invite and include the consent template + a one-page case-story outline beforehand.
